In Buenos Aires, a woman named Sofia is finishing her late afternoon tea at a cozy café in Palermo. As she stirs the remaining sugar into her cup, her thoughts wander to the bustling streets outside. She considers her evening plans — the tango class she has every Wednesday at the historic milonga down the street. She had been going there for months, not just for the dance but for the company she found among fellow tangueros.

Her mind shifts to her work at the design agency. She has been feeling discontent with the routine and wonders if it's time for a change. Perhaps she should pursue the freelance path, which would give her more freedom to travel and work from anywhere. The idea excites her, but also fills her with uncertainty and a touch of apprehension.

As she finishes her tea, Sofia decides she will take the first step tomorrow by contacting a few colleagues who have made the switch successfully. She envisages setting up a small home office by the window where she could draw inspiration from the view of the jacaranda trees lining the street. Tonight, she'll focus on the dance, lose herself in the music, and let her partner lead her in the rhythm and tradition of Buenos Aires, forgetting about decisions to be made, at least for a little while.
